column1: Day 1: whisk the biga flour and yeast in a large bowl, stir in the room-temperature water, cover tightly and leave at room temperature 8–24 hours.
Day 2: in another large bowl (or stand mixer with dough hook) whisk the yeast into the warm water and let sit 5–10 minutes to dissolve.
Add the biga, flour and salt and mix until evenly moistened with no dry pockets. The dough will be very wet and sticky.
With an oiled hand or spatula, lift one edge of the dough, stretch it up and fold it over to the opposite side. Turn the bowl a quarter turn and repeat for 8 folds total. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Repeat the stretch-and-fold and 30 minute rest three more times (4 rounds total), then refrigerate the covered dough at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours.
Heavily flour the counter, scrape the dough out, flour the top and pat into roughly a 10x7 inch rectangle.
Cut into 8 rolls or 2 loaves with a floured bench scraper and move them to floured parchment at least 2 inches apart, reshaping gently.
Dust the tops with flour, cover with a towel and proof 1 hour.
Meanwhile set racks in the center and bottom of the oven, put a baking sheet on the center rack and preheat to 450°F (232°C) for about an hour.
Fill a metal pan with several cups of ice. Mist the rolls with water, slide the parchment onto the hot baking sheet, place the ice pan on the bottom rack and shut the door quickly.
Bake 20–25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding, or 205–210°F (96–99°C) inside.
Cool at least 45 minutes before slicing.
